whatItFakes: The smallest change stored as a moment.
why: Defined as the smallest row of the 1967 scale (11 units) and carrying the 2021 replication's 22 as the other end of its spread (Oct 16, 2026). A yearly count of stored moments to check it against was not found, so the floor is a scale definition, not a calibrated count.
replacement: An owner answer or a tested calibration for the same quantity.

whatItFakes: The impact at which a moment takes over the screen.
why: A pacing choice by the owner, which no study measures (Oct 16, 2026 research); the marriage anchor is 50 units on both the 1967 scale and its 2021 replication, so the line holds if the scale is updated. Stays TUNABLE against play.
replacement: An owner answer or a tested calibration for the same quantity.

whatItFakes: How much the watched person's own death counts.
why: The watched person's own death is a design weight at the top of the scale; no stress scale rates one's own death (Oct 16, 2026 research). Stays TUNABLE against play.
replacement: An owner answer or a tested calibration for the same quantity.

whatItFakes: How much sociability raises a tie change.
why: Bounded above by the design's one quarter with 0 not contradicted (Oct 16, 2026 research: personality did not consistently moderate responses to life events). No coefficient exists.
replacement: An owner answer or a tested calibration for the same quantity.

whatItFakes: How much avoiding risk raises a money loss.
why: Bounded in size by the design's one quarter, sign from loss aversion, 0 not contradicted (Oct 16, 2026 research). No coefficient exists.
replacement: An owner answer or a tested calibration for the same quantity.

whatItFakes: When a contact is labeled a renewal (labeling only).
why: Labels a contact a renewal and decides no outcome; it follows from the half-lives (Oct 16, 2026 research). Stays TUNABLE.
replacement: An owner answer or a tested calibration for the same quantity.

whatItFakes: Standing ties for family and a shared home, the partner tie, and the fading discount.
why: The partner tie is now scaled from the spouse-to-close-family ratio on the 1967 scale (0.79; 0.57 on the 2021 replication). No source ranks sibling, grandparent, grandchild or shared-home ties or measures the fading discount; they stay the October 8, 2026 design weights until the replay calibration.
replacement: A calibration of thread importance against recorded closeness in replayed lives.

whatItFakes: How fast closeness fades without contact for friends and relatives.
why: No study reports a half-life for closeness without contact; Roberts and Dunbar (2015) give direction only, and 18 months is their study's length. Tagged TUNABLE (CTO, October 10, 2026). Resolved: Checked against Roberts and Dunbar (2015): their retention converts to 526 and 1,078 days, within 4 percent of 548 and 1,096; the kin value now equals the core's 1,095 and both rows carry the converted spread (Oct 16, 2026).
replacement: A half-life calibrated against network turnover over years (for example Mollenhorst, Volker and Flap 2014, once checked), the target P15 uses.

whatItFakes: The director recomputes each event's feeling with the core's exported appraisal function instead of reading the appraisal the core applied.
why: The core keeps only the resulting mood and stress (src/core2/modules/life.ts:319); hook requested from SOL-1258.
replacement: Read the appraisal receipt the core passes with each event.

whatItFakes: Tie changes are read once at the end of each day, losing their order within the day.
why: Relationship changes emit no event (src/core2/state.ts:561); hook requested from SOL-1258.
replacement: A relationship change notice from the core.

whatItFakes: Lies, favors and promises are kept-fact kinds with no producer, so none is ever recorded.
why: The new core has no act or event that records a lie, a favor or a promise.
replacement: Producers in the core's conversation and favor modules, listed in producedBy.

whatItFakes: How fast an anniversary's weight falls away from the date.
why: The owner's answer 7. The only measured window is one week and no study calibrates the half-life (Oct 16, 2026 research).
replacement: A calibration against when people recall shared events.

whatItFakes: Impacts for recorded past facts, read from stress-scale rows rather than measured changes.
why: The eight past-fact weights are the 1967 Holmes and Rahe rows; the 2021 replication gives higher values for seven (carried as each row's spread). Choosing a vintage is the owner's call, since the floor and the interrupt line move with it.
replacement: Past moments measured from replayed lives once the life-replay harness runs on the new core.

whatItFakes: How long a watched person keeps every moment in full, and how many older moments they keep one by one.
why: No study sets either; chosen so memory stays about the same size across a year while the recent season stays whole.
replacement: A calibration against what people bring up in play (M4-05) and the owner's grading of the journal.

whatItFakes: The journal's line templates, written by hand instead of composed from mined real speech.
why: The first new-core journal needs words now; the templates copy only recorded facts and hold no feeling words. Resolved Oct 14 (words/mined-banks-in-play): the journal is worded from data/english/parts/journal.json via src/director/mined/journal-bank.ts; journal.json is deleted, its sentence-free rows live in journal-rows.json, and unworded moments are left out.
replacement: Lines composed from the mined first-person corpus in the speech research, refined by the owner's grades (M4-03).

whatItFakes: Conversation line templates written by hand instead of composed from mined real speech.
why: The first new-core conversations need words now; each template copies only recorded facts. Resolved Oct 14 (words/mined-banks-in-play): the director's conversation words are mined public-domain sentences from data/english/parts/conversation.json via src/director/mined/conversation-bank.ts; the hand-written bank is deleted and a moment no mined sentence covers is left unsaid.
replacement: Lines composed from the mined speech corpus and register cards, refined by the owner's grades (M4-02).

whatItFakes: Scene narration templates written by hand instead of composed from mined real speech and narration.
why: The first new-core scenes need words now; each template copies only recorded facts. Resolved Oct 14 (words/mined-banks-in-play): scenes are worded from data/english/parts/scene-words.json via src/director/mined/scene-bank.ts; scene-words.json is deleted and unmined settings are left unnarrated.
replacement: Narration composed from the mined corpus, refined by the owner's grades (M4-03).

whatItFakes: The filing clerk's line templates, written by hand instead of composed from mined real speech.
why: Step 3 needs the clerk's words now; each template copies only GOV's filing records. Resolved Oct 14 (words/mined-banks-in-play): the clerk speaks mined sentences from data/english/parts/filing-visit.json via src/director/mined/filing-bank.ts; filing-visit.json is deleted; fees and signatures stay record data and control names.
replacement: Clerk lines composed from mined public-counter speech and refined by the owner's grades (M4-02).

whatItFakes: The templates people use to bring up a change and say who caused it, and the one trait that sends blame toward authority.
why: M4-05's first version needs words and a blame lean now; each template copies only what the speaker heard. Resolved Oct 14 (words/mined-banks-in-play): bring-it-up lines are mined from data/english/parts/bring-it-up.json via src/director/mined/scene-bank.ts; bring-it-up.json is deleted and the unmined told-blame line is left out.
replacement: Lines composed from mined speech; blame leaning on views, trust and the person's own experience of each official (M4-05).

whatItFakes: Which of the bill catalog's policy names read as an action the President can ask Congress for, listed by their first word.
why: The opening address needs the President's own issues as a {goal} now; the catalog names some questions as actions ("raise minimum wage") and some as things ("paid family leave").
replacement: An action phrase on each policy question in OPUS-GOV's bill catalog, or a mined goal phrase per question from OPUS-WORDS.

whatItFakes: The register card the President's opening address composes under: election night's public-address card stands in for a President's address.
why: The engine has no register card for a State of the Union or an inaugural address yet (docs/coordination/words.md); the mined sentences need a public-address card to compose.
replacement: A President's-address register card in src/english/speech-registers.ts (OPUS-PEOPLE).

whatItFakes: The register card the evening news composes under: the press briefing's card stands in for a newscast.
why: The engine has no register card for a newscast yet (docs/coordination/words.md); the opening's evening news composes now.
replacement: A newscast register card in src/english/speech-registers.ts (OPUS-PEOPLE).

whatItFakes: Nobody works the polling place: the election-day scene shows the voter and the household members who may vote, with no poll workers.
why: The elections engine records no polling place for a precinct and no one who works it; the scene's poll-workers role needs that record. Resolved Oct 16, 2026 (elections-poll-workers): the voting engine's pollingPlaceOf names who works each precinct's polls (named adults ranked by duty, interest in politics and free hours, as many as EAVS 2022's poll workers per voting location), and the polling-place visit carries pollingPlaceId and pollWorkerIds from it.
replacement: GOV's polling-place record (`polling-place:<precinct>` with `pollWorkerIds`), read by the poll-workers fill.

whatItFakes: How many choices a conversation turn offers: only the distinct answer moves the mined bank words, one to three per turn, with no unrelated subject tacked on to reach a count.
why: Two owner rulings pull apart: Sept 29, 'options come from context, 3 to 5 at a time'; Oct 14 (grading batch 6), a reply's second move must follow from the first. The newer one is applied until the owner rules. Resolved Oct 14 (owner ruling, afternoon): a conversation always offers four replies ranked by the player's traits (conversation.reply-reach), with 'say nothing' a smaller control beside them (sayNothing, the bench's Say nothing button); each move is offered plainly and carried on to the subject it leads to, and every acknowledgment is its own reply.
replacement: The owner's ruling: either fewer choices are right, or OPUS-WORDS mines more answer moves per subject until three to five follow naturally.

whatItFakes: How long ago a recorded event still makes something two people talk about, and lets someone not in the room be asked after.
why: The owner ruled what a talk opens on (Oct 14, 2026, night), not how long news stays news; one season is a guess checked against played talks.
replacement: A tested calibration against played talks, or an owner answer.

whatItFakes: How much the President's address weighs as a talk's topic, times the speaker's political engagement.
why: The owner ruled public news comes up only for people who follow politics closely (Oct 14, 2026, night); the size is a guess kept below a life event's.
replacement: A tested calibration against played talks, or an owner answer.

whatItFakes: The office scene picks its target only among members whose position reads the views engine (town bodies' full-person members); state and federal officials are skipped.
why: An official's position (officialParts) reads their officials record, not the views engine's stances, so a case made to them moves nothing. Resolved Oct 16 (director-reach): officialParts now adds the views engine's case shift to an official's own stand, and the scene no longer skips officials.
replacement: Done: officialParts reads the views engine's stance on each question (src/core2/modules/officials.ts, caseShift in views.ts), and the scene's target filter is removed; shown in src/director/office-scene-levels.test.ts.

whatItFakes: The clerk who takes a filing is left unfilled in a scene: the filing visit shows the player and the office's title, with no clerk in the room.
why: An office in the new core holds a title (the county clerk, the municipal clerk), not a person; no record names who staffs a filing counter. Resolved Oct 16 (gov-clerk-person): filingClerkFor reads an elected clerk, the town's appointed city clerk or the county government's listed clerk, and the clerk fill returns that person.
replacement: A clerk's office has a clerk: a full person on the town's payroll or an elected holder, read by the clerk fill (pool item gov-clerk-person).

whatItFakes: The person who tells someone a law changed their check is the head of the outlet whose story taught them; no record names who told them in person, and a notice from the probate court has no teller at all.
why: The news module records which story a person heard and its outlet, not who retold it. Whether a person, a friend or a reporter, should be the teller is the owner's call. Resolved Oct 19 (director-law-learned-from-outlet): the owner ruled on Oct 16 that the source is the story or feed that reached the person, so no teller is filled.
replacement: The owner's ruling: either the person who retold the story (the speech engine's retelling record) or an outlet's reporter, read by the teller fill.
resolution: Ruled by the owner on Oct 16: a person learns that a law changed their money mostly from the news or a feed, not from a person. The law-takes-effect scene is now the reached person's alone, caused by the learned-effect record, which cites the story that reached them (learnedFrom); the teller role and fill are gone, and a person is in the scene only where a conversation record shows one.
